See also: Couscous

English

[edit]

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • cuscousou, cuscusu (dated)

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from French couscous, from Arabic كُسْكُس (kuskus), from a Berber language. First use appears c. 1593.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • (UK) IPA(key): /ˈkʊs.kʊs/, /ˈkuːs.kuːs/
  • Audio (Southern England):(file)
  • Audio (Southern England):(file)
  • (US) IPA(key): /ˈkus.kus/

Noun

[edit]

couscous (countable and uncountable, plural couscouses)

  1. A pasta of North African origin made of crushed and steamed semolina.
    • 2012, Laini Taylor, Days of Blood & Starlight, →ISBN:
      Karou took the plate of couscous and vegetables.

Quotations

[edit]
  • For more quotations using this term, see Citations:couscous.

Derived terms

[edit]
  • couscoussier
  • Israeli couscous
  • pearl couscous
  • pearled couscous
